title: Ulyana and the Static
premise: On the generation ship Halcyon, Marguerite Vasquez investigates 'impossible accidents'—deaths the ship's systems insist never happened. The truth: two cryogenic archives hold rival halves of humanity, and a faction is quietly erasing one of them. When the colony's children begin sharing a dream sent by the sleeping minds themselves, Marguerite's hidden role as the ship's last authorized arbiter surfaces, forcing her to choose which archive wakes. She chooses neither intact: she merges the manifests at terrible cost, waking a hybrid humanity that must live with what was done in its name.
about_author: Casper Brightwater is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years adjudicating losses at sea before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the machinery that decides who survives.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Marguerite files her fortieth impossible-accident report—a hydroponics tech who died twice on paper and not at all in fact. POV: Marguerite. Establishes her methodical invisibility and the ship's decaying bureaucracy. Emotional beat: weary competence masking dread that the numbers no longer add up.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: A schoolteacher reports forty children drawing identical images: a door underwater, someone knocking. Marguerite interviews them; one girl describes Marguerite's own childhood cryo-dream word for word. POV: Marguerite with a child's testimony interlude. Beat: uncanny recognition—the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: Actuarial Ghosts
chapters.summary: Marguerite traces the impossible accidents to Archive B's life-support draw, discovering hundreds of sleepers whose records were voided. Her supervisor, Okafor, warns her to stop filing. POV: Marguerite. Beat: first glimpse of deliberate erasure; fear replaces curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Ship Owes
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Marguerite's mother signed the original arbitration covenant, then vanished into cryo rather than choose. POV: alternating Marguerite present-day and mother's recovered log entries. Beat: inheritance as burden—she realizes she is the covenant's executor.

chapters.title: The Quiet Faction
chapters.summary: Marguerite infiltrates an engineering deck and finds Okafor's people purging Archive B pods under a mandate forged decades ago. She escapes with a data-slate but loses her anonymity. POV: Marguerite, tight thriller pacing. Beat: power revealed as corruption wearing procedure's face.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: The dream spreads to adults; riots flare between crew loyal to each archive. The girl from Chapter 2 falls comatose, dreaming harder than the rest. POV: ensemble—Okafor, the teacher, the girl's father. Beat: society fracturing along lines most people didn't know existed.

chapters.title: Terms of Settlement
chapters.summary: Okafor offers Marguerite a deal: ratify Archive A's survival and her mother's pod stays powered. Marguerite visits her mother's frozen body and finds the covenant's true clause—neither half may be chosen alone. POV: Marguerite. Beat: temptation, then refusal; the price of survival named aloud.

chapters.title: Every Name Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Marguerite broadcasts both archives' full manifests ship-wide and begins the arbitration rite, reading names while factions stand down or don't. Saboteurs cut power mid-rite. POV: Marguerite with chorus voices. Climax beat: she invokes the merge protocol, betting everything on a third option.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: The merged awakening begins—thousands rise disoriented, fewer than either side wanted, more than either expected. Okafor surrenders rather than kill children of both lines. POV: shifting to the awakened and the girl who wakes from her coma speaking two languages. Beat: grief and relief entangled.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Again
chapters.summary: One year later, Marguerite returns to investigating—but now the accidents are honest ones, mourned openly. She files her mother's final report and lets herself be seen. POV: Marguerite. Resolution beat: inheritance transformed into stewardship; visibility chosen, not forced.
